explain.say: Imagine you are stuck on an island, surrounded by seawater you cannot drink. Could you make it safe? Look at the board. First, you heat the seawater in a flask.

explain.say: See the steam? Water boils at 100 °C and turns to vapour, which means water as a gas. Salt needs over 1,400 °C to boil, so it stays in the flask. Can you guess where the vapour goes next?

explain.say: Into this cold tube, called a condenser. Cold water flows around the outside of it. Look at how the hot vapour meets the cold glass. What happens when your warm breath meets a cold window?

explain.say: It condenses! Watch the particles on the board lose energy, slow down and huddle into drops of liquid water. That is condensing, the opposite of boiling. Is this water salty or pure, do you think?

Pure! Well done, you made drinking water. The clean water that drips out is called the distillate, and the salt stays behind in the flask. Wow: some huge plants in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates use this idea to make drinking water for millions of people.

faq.q: Why does the salt stay behind?
faq.a: Water boils at 100 °C, but salt only boils at about 1,413 °C. So only the water turns into vapour and leaves the flask.
asks: Why doesn't salt go into the condenser?

faq.a: A condenser is a glass tube with cold water flowing around it. The hot vapour inside cools down, condenses into liquid, and runs out of the end.
The distillate is the pure liquid collected after distillation, here pure water.
Simple distillation gets a pure liquid out of a solution, like water from seawater. Fractional distillation separates liquids with different boiling points, like the parts of crude oil.

faq.q: Why is distilled water used in steam irons?
faq.a: Distilled water has no dissolved minerals, so it leaves no white scale behind. That keeps irons and car batteries working well.

facts: Simple distillation separates a solvent from a solution by boiling the solvent and then condensing it.
Sodium chloride melts at 801 °C and boils at about 1,413 °C.
